information.expert_knowledge:
Data validation ranges based on clinical literature:

baseline_heartRate (Baseline Heart Rate) column:
Accepts values 20-280 beats per minute (bpm) based on clinical evidence. Normal adult heart rate ranges from 60-100 bpm according to Avram et al. (2019). The lower bound of 20 bpm accounts for extreme bradycardia cases, with Mangrum & DiMarco (2000) defining sleep bradycardia at 30-35 bpm and Lesser et al. (2003) documenting severe bradycardia below 40 bpm. The upper bound captures extreme tachycardia, with Patti et al. (2025) reporting supraventricular tachycardia in the range of 150-220 bpm and Page et al. (2016) documenting Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia exceeding 250 bpm.

heartRate (Current Heart Rate) column:
Accepts values 20-280 bpm, using the same clinical evidence and rationale as baseline heart rate.

baseline_spo2 (Baseline Oxygen Saturation) column:
Accepts values 65-100% based on clinical evidence. Normal SpO2 levels range from 95-100%, with values below 90% considered hypoxemia according to Torp et al. (2017). The lower bound of 65% accounts for extreme hypoxemia cases documented in medical literature. Tobin et al. (2020) note that oxygen saturations of 80-85% are considered life-threatening, and report that individuals at high altitude (top of Mount Evans near Denver) can experience oxygen saturations of 65% for prolonged periods, establishing this as a physiologically possible albeit critically low value.

spo2 (Current Oxygen Saturation) column:
Accepts values 65-100%, using the same clinical evidence and rationale as baseline oxygen saturation.

age column:
Accepts values 0-120 years. This range encompasses the full human lifespan, with the upper bound accounting for documented cases of extreme longevity.

sexe column:
Accepts binary values 0 (female) and 1 (male). This represents the biological sex categories used in the training dataset from Swaminathan et al. (2017).

baseline_height column:
Accepts values 0-250 cm based on anthropometric data. The lower bound of 0 serves as a technical placeholder. The upper bound of 250 cm accounts for extreme cases of gigantism and the tallest recorded humans in medical literature.

baseline_weight column:
Accepts values 0-500 kg based on clinical observations. The lower bound of 0 serves as a technical placeholder. The upper bound of 500 kg captures extreme cases documented in clinical literature.

baseline_bmi column:
Accepts values 0-80 kg/m² based on clinical classifications. The lower bound of 0 serves as a technical placeholder. The upper bound of 80 kg/m² accounts for extreme cases documented in medical literature, though such values are exceptionally rare.

baseline_copd (Baseline COPD GOLD Stage) column:
Accepts categorical values 1-4 representing COPD severity stages according to the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) classification system. Stage 1 represents mild COPD, Stage 2 moderate, Stage 3 severe, and Stage 4 very severe COPD.

symp_worsening (Symptom Worsening) column:
Accepts categorical values 0-3 representing the duration of symptom deterioration. According to the model documentation: 0 = No worsening, 1 = Worsening for the last 24 hours, 2 = Worsening for 1-3 days, 3 = Worsening for more than 3 days.

symp_breath (Shortness of Breath) column:
Accepts categorical values 1-3 representing dyspnea severity relative to baseline. According to the model documentation: 1 = Less than usual, 2 = Same as usual, 3 = More than usual.

symp_cough column:
Accepts categorical values 1-3 representing cough frequency relative to baseline. According to the model documentation: 1 = Less than usual, 2 = Same as usual, 3 = More than usual.

symp_sputum (Sputum Volume and Color) column:
Accepts categorical values 0-3 representing sputum changes. According to the model documentation: 0 = No change, 1 = Change in sputum color only, 2 = Increased sputum volume only, 3 = Both increased volume and color change.

Note on Missing Data:
According to Swaminathan et al. (2017), the model is designed to handle partially missing patient data. Optional fields (baseline_copd, baseline_heartRate, baseline_spo2, heartRate, spo2) can have a value of 0 indicating 'unknown' without compromising the model's ability to generate predictions. However, required fields (age, sexe, baseline_height, baseline_weight, baseline_bmi, and all symptom questions: symp_worsening, symp_breath, symp_cough, symp_sputum) must contain valid values for the model to function properly.
information.statistical_analysis:
Statistical Analysis performs comprehensive data quality validation through five key checks:

1. Missing Values: Detects null/NaN values throughout the dataset, counting occurrences per column and identifying specific row indices with missing data.

2. Column Consistency: Validates that all expected columns from the configuration are present while identifying any missing required columns or unexpected extra columns.

3. Data Types: Ensures each column's data type matches the configuration specifications, verifying that numeric columns contain numeric data and categorical columns have appropriate discrete values.

4. Duplicate Column Names: Identifies columns with identical names and reports their occurrence to detect potential schema issues.

5. Duplicate Rows: Finds completely identical rows within the dataset and reports their indices.
information.adversarial_evaluation: Adversarial Evaluation compares model performance between synthetic and real-world datasets by calculating four classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score) on both data types. The evaluation generates predictions using the Dockerized COPowereD model, then computes performance differences in percentage points (pp, synthetic minus real-world). This approach identifies whether synthetic data maintains comparable predictive utility to real-world data for model training and validation.
